title: Six Llamas: Comparative Religious Ethics Through LoRA-Adapted Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Fine-tuning a base large language model (Llama-3.1-8B) on five distinct religious corpora (Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Buddhism) using LoRA, and comparing the models' responses to a standardized battery of 17 ethical prompts to see how religious training data systematically biases moral reasoning.

Evaluating model responses across moral dilemmas, game-theoretic scenarios, and public policy questions, and mapping them onto Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) to identify differing cultural frameworks, prosocial orientations, and communal versus individualistic biases.

Comparing the unmodified, instruction-tuned base model's responses against the religiously fine-tuned variants to identify the base model's inherent secular, utilitarian, and consequentialist biases introduced during the safety and alignment training process.
